correctness.rationale: Tracing equality through the standard construction behind \(\gamma_{\rm cer}\le\gamma+|S_1|\le2\gamma\) forces every vertex of a suitable minimum dominating set to be a weak support with exactly its private leaf outside the set, hence a corona. The fixed-order parity bounds then follow from \(\gamma\le n/2\), the impossibility of certified domination number \(n-1\), and the published characterizations of \(\gamma_{\rm cer}=n\) and \(\gamma_{\rm cer}=n-2\). The Graph-Atlas artifact exhaustively matches the theorem through order seven but is corroborative only.

evidence: The 2016 source already characterizes connected graphs with certified domination number \(n\) as coronas and with value \(n-2\) as diadems apart from small cycles.
These statements cover the extremal structures needed for both parity cases.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The published large-value theory is broad enough to dominate the fixed-order classification once the elementary order bounds are inserted.

evidence: Equality \(\gamma_{\rm cer}=2\gamma\) forces equality in the half-shadowed-support construction; hence every minimum-set vertex has exactly one private leaf outside and all other neighbors inside, producing a corona.

For odd order, a hypothetical larger gap would require the impossible value \(n-1\); equality at the next value invokes the published \(n-2\) diadem characterization. For even order, equality invokes the published \(n\) corona characterization.

originality.rationale: The final theorem is covered at the required implication level by the foundational certified-domination paper. Its Theorem 3.3 proof gives the half-shadowed weak-support construction, Corollary 3.5 gives \(\gamma_{\rm cer}\le2\gamma\) with corona sharpness, Theorem 5.3 characterizes \(\gamma_{\rm cer}=n\) by coronas in the connected case, and Section 5.1 characterizes \(\gamma_{\rm cer}=n-2\) by diadems for connected graphs of order at least five. Following equality through the already-published proof yields the factor-two converse with no new nonstandard lemma; the parity gap classification is then a short corollary of those published large-value theorems and the classical domination bound.

value.rationale: The parity formula and corona/diadem packaging are neat, but once the published factor-two proof and the published \(n\) and \(n-2\) classifications are assembled, the remaining work is a short equality-case trace and classical order bound. Under the shared value bar, that is a routine corollary rather than a separate motivated mathematical gap.
residual_risks: The statement remains useful as a concise corollary package.

final_claim: For connected graphs, the maximum fixed-order gap \(\gamma_{\rm cer}-\gamma\) is \(n/2\) for even \(n\) and \((n-3)/2\) for odd \(n\); the proposed equality classification uses coronas and diadems and includes the factor-two statement \(\gamma_{\rm cer}=2\gamma\) exactly for coronas.
limitations: The rejection is scientific prior-implication coverage, not a correctness or access failure.
